issues.description: default_raise sentinel and its comment are stale after dropping 3.9
issues.detail: The comment above TransactionEndpointRequest still says 'this is for < 3.10 compatibility', and chia/wallet/wallet_request_types.py keeps default_raise() with comment 'for < 3.10 compatibility'. Now that kw_only is unconditional and required-without-default fields are expressible directly, the literate explanation is wrong and the helper is arguably vestigial. State the invariant the reader needs: either keep default_raise with an honest rationale (e.g., 'streamable's @dataclass requires every field to have a default, so we synthesize one that raises'), or remove it. Leaving a misleading comment in foundational request types is exactly the kind of unreadability this lens flags.

issues.description: Ruff UP007/UP035/UP045 suppressed wholesale with a TODO and no plan
issues.detail: ruff.toml now ignores UP045, UP007, UP035 with the comment 'TODO: Remove these - it's a lot of errors'. The PR description states Union/Optional should migrate to A | B / A | None, but the lint that would enforce that is disabled indefinitely. Either land the migration in this PR (the whole point of the 3.10 floor) or file a tracking issue and reference it in the comment. A TODO with no owner and no deadline is how style debt becomes permanent; for code meant to be read, that matters.

issues.description: Amazon Linux / Rocky install scripts run 'dnf search' in a build step
issues.detail: test-install-scripts.yml now runs 'dnf update -y; dnf search python3.12; dnf install git python3.12 -y' on both Amazon Linux and Rocky. 'dnf search' is purely informational and writes to stdout; if it's debug scaffolding it should be removed before merge, and if it's deliberate diagnostics it should be commented as such. Also 'dnf update -y' on every CI run is a large, unpinned operation that changes what's tested between runs and slows the job — usually you want 'dnf install -y' alone, or 'dnf makecache' if you need fresh metadata. State the invariant: what does this step guarantee, and why does it need a full update?

issues.description: itertools.pairwise swap is a clean win; worth a one-line invariant comment
issues.detail: Replacing zip(ordered, ordered[1:]) with itertools.pairwise(ordered) is correct and avoids the O(n) slice allocation — a real (small) constant-factor win and more readable. Since 'sane' is a test invariant checker, a single-line comment stating the invariant ('every adjacent pair in sorted order satisfies a.before(b)') would make the function self-documenting at literate-programming grade. Nit, but this is exactly the kind of place the comment is cheap.

issues.description: find_python loop in install.sh still searches legacy compact form '39' is gone but ordering deserves a comment
issues.detail: The shell loop 'for V in 312 3.12 311 3.11 310 3.10 3;' correctly drops 39/3.9. The invariant — 'prefer highest available minor, fall back to bare python3 last' — is not stated and the dual-form (312 and 3.12) exists because some distros name the binary one way and some the other. A one-line comment would make this readable without running it; right now a maintainer has to reverse-engineer the convention.

issues.description: install.sh version-range check still references '< 7' lower bound
issues.detail: The guard 'if [ "$PYTHON_MAJOR_VER" -ne "3" ] || [ "$PYTHON_MINOR_VER" -lt "7" ] || [ "$PYTHON_MINOR_VER" -ge "13" ]; then' keeps the lower bound at 7 while the error message and project floor are now 3.10. The user-visible string is correct ('>= 3.10'), but the executable check accepts 3.7/3.8/3.9 silently as 'fine' and then would presumably fail later at pip install when requires-python kicks in. Tighten the numeric guard to match the message — that's the readable, correct version of this check.

issues.description: conditions.py 'pragma: no cover' comment removed but the branch is now structurally dead
issues.detail: In parse_timelock_info, the else branch is a bare 'continue' inside an elif chain that exhausts the Condition subclasses checked above. With 3.9 gone, the coverage tooling note is correctly removed, but the branch itself is only reachable if a new Condition subclass is added without updating this function. Worth either an assert/raise to fail loudly on an unknown Condition (preserving the invariant 'every Condition we care about here is handled') or a one-line comment stating that this is the 'ignore unrelated condition types' case. Right now the bare 'continue' reads as accidental rather than deliberate.

review.summary: RIGOROUS on the mechanical core: the version-gate cleanups in cmd_classes.py and wallet_request_types.py are exactly the kind of dead-conditional removal that a 3.9 drop should produce, and the kw_only=True normalization actually improves readability — fewer code paths, fewer 'pragma: no cover' apologies, clearer dataclass intent. NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT on the leftovers: default_raise and the 'TransactionEndpointRequest is for < 3.10' comment in wallet_request_types.py are now stale and should be either rewritten with an honest rationale (Streamable forces defaults) or removed. UNDER-AUDITED on the lint policy: ruff.toml suppresses UP007/UP035/UP045 with a bare TODO, which contradicts the PR description's stated goal of migrating to A | B / A | None — that's style debt with no owner. The CI script changes (dnf update -y; dnf search python3.12) look like debug residue and deserve a second look before merge. The itertools.pairwise swap is a clean, small constant-factor win and the right call.
